title: Pullback preserves invertibility over the locally invertible open
statement: Let $W,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $\varphi:M\to N$ any morphism of $\mathcal O_W$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $h:T\to W$ have topological image contained in $U_\varphi$ [def-sc-module-map-iso-locus]. Then the tensor-formula pullback $h^*\varphi$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is an isomorphism. No finite type or local freeness condition on $M,N$ is imposed.

source.place: Composition of pullback; Tag 04TN, isomorphisms are local

proof.text: The inverse images under h of all opens appearing in the defining supremum cover T. Prove the cover equality pointwise using mem_moduleMapIsoLocus and image containment.

Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies tensor pullback with Mathlib pullback. Composition of pullback, morphismRestrict_ι, and pullbackCongr show that on each inverse-image open the map is a further pullback of an isomorphism. RestrictFunctorIsoPullback and overFunctorEquiv identify this with the over restriction.

Forget to abelian sheaves, apply Mathlib Sheaf.isIso_of_coversTop to the cover, then reflect isomorphisms through SheafOfModules.toSheaf. This glues the local inverses, including for the empty test scheme.

mathlib_searches.query: A morphism of finite locally free sheaves is invertible on an open subscheme, and arbitrary pullback is invertible exactly when its image lies in this open
mathlib_searches.results: Eight results including Scheme.Modules.Hom.isIso_iff_isIso_app, isLocalIso_iff and scheme open-immersion app lemmas; none states the requested locus construction, compactness or reflection criterion.
QuasiCompact and quasiCompact_iff_forall_isAffineOpen supply the generic conversion, not compactness of the module-map locus.

No module-map iso-locus definition or vector-bundle universal locus theorem in Mathlib or the library. Mathlib has pullback composition, restrictFunctorIsoPullback, overFunctorEquiv and Sheaf.isIso_of_coversTop; used to prove the preservation direction. Blueprint/DAG search finds the parent universal locus, not its strictly smaller components.
